## Before class

Read Speegle and Clair, *Probability, Statistics, and Data*,
[§§8.1–8.5](https://probstatsdata.com/HTCI.html#samplingdistmean).
We focus on confidence intervals in §§8.1–8.2 and the assumptions discussed
in §8.5. Hypothesis tests and one-sided inference receive a fuller treatment
in the next seminar. Bring your laptop. **B4 is due at 1:30 p.m.**

## During the seminar

A difference in turnout motivates the move from point estimates to intervals.
We derive interval endpoints from a standardized statistic, then use repeated
samples to see coverage: the intervals vary while the population parameter
stays fixed. Confidence levels, standard errors, and sample size determine
interval width.

The studentized CLT supplies the general large-sample argument. The exact
$t$ result for Normal observations is an additional special case. We compare
$t$ and Normal cutoffs and examine how skewness and dependence can change
actual coverage. The final examples connect intervals to plotted error bars.
